variants.note: Brick. mudejar's structural and ornamental material throughout; one of moorish-andalusian's two named wall materials.
Tapia. moorish-andalusian's other named wall material; not attested for mudejar, whose own text is brick-centred throughout.

construction_type.rule: Massive load-bearing wall construction in brick or, in Moorish work specifically, rammed earth (tapia). No framed or veneer alternative appears in either member's own text.

thickness.note: Range given is the overlap of both members' own stated figures (600-900mm and 500-700mm respectively); the full union is roughly 20-35in. Moorish-andalusian's own text ties the thickness explicitly to a 12-hour thermal lag.

wall_thickness_masonry.rule: Mass wall roughly 20-35 in (500-900 mm) thick depending on member; the shared, safely-overlapping core is about 24-28 in (600-700 mm).

variants.note: A rectangular moulded frame enclosing the arch, so the arch never floats free on the wall. Hard constraint in mudejar (c03: 'any arched opening of consequence must be enclosed by an alfiz'); explicit diagnostic tell in moorish-andalusian.

window_surround_masonry.rule: Any significant arched opening — window or door alike — is enclosed by an alfiz, a rectangular moulded frame that squares off the arch against the wall plane. An arch left to float free on the wall is outside the grammar of both members.

window_grouping_rule.rule: External openings toward the street are minimal, small, and set high, above head height; the building's real fenestration faces inward onto the court. This is not a stylistic preference but a hard rule in both members.

street_wall_glazing_max_pct.note: Explicit hard constraint on moorish-andalusian: openings in the outer street wall not to exceed 5% of its area. mudejar states the same principle qualitatively ('external openings small and high; large openings face the patio', mudejar.c05) without its own percentage figure.

order.rule: No classical order and no absolute module govern the composition. Setting-out is geometric (compass-and-straightedge construction from a square or a star polygon), not order-derived.
order.note: moorish-andalusian's own governing_logic: 'There is no order and no absolute module: the setting-out is a compass-and-straightedge procedure.' No pack in the 36-pack proportion library models this Islamic geometric system either — see docs/reports/wp-4.1-proportion-pack-bindings.md, which left both moorish-andalusian and mudejar entirely unbound at the style level for exactly this reason.

entablature.rule: Arches are carried directly on columns or piers in an arcade, never on a stone entablature. No classical entablature run exists in either member's own vocabulary.
entablature.note: moorish-andalusian diagnostic_tells: 'columns... carrying brick or plaster arches, not stone entablatures.' Consistent with the wider corpus convention that classical-apparatus slots are bound only within the classical stream; this family sits outside it.

variants.note: Azulejo or alicatado tile from the floor to a datum height, above which the wall changes material and pattern entirely.

dado_height.note: Overlap of both members' stated tile-dado heights, converted to inches; the full union is roughly 47-79in (1.2-2.0m).

wainscot.rule: A glazed tile dado runs from the floor to a horizontal datum, above which the wall surface changes material (to carved plaster in Moorish work, to brick or plain render in Mudejar work) and pattern completely, with a horizontal band usually marking the transition.
wainscot.note: moorish-andalusian's own hard constraint (c03) states this stratification as a strict rule with three tiers (tile/plaster/timber); mudejar's own text and typical_ratios confirm the tile dado's presence and height band but do not restate the full three-tier stratification as explicitly, so only the tile-dado fact itself — not the full stratification rule — is bound here as genuinely shared.

value.source: moorish-andalusian description ('reached from the court rather than from internal corridors')
value.note: Explicit for moorish-andalusian. mudejar's own text does not restate this directly (its focus is church/tower typology rather than domestic planning) but its courtyard-full and townhouse-row massing affinities describe the same single-pile, court-entered organisation by extension; confidence held at medium for mudejar's share of this fact.

circulation_parti.rule: Rooms are entered from the court or its surrounding portico, not from an internal corridor.

value.source: moorish-andalusian description ('single-pile ranges around the court'); mudejar massing_affinities note ('fully enclosed courts with single-pile ranges')

depth_and_pile.rule: Ranges are single-pile around the court, so every room can be cross-ventilated or lit from the court.

street_relationship.rule: A high, blind or near-blind wall faces the street; the sole entry is a single controlled door. In Moorish work the passage is bent or set off-axis specifically so the court is never visible from the street.
street_relationship.note: moorish-andalusian states this explicitly and in detail ('a single door, often set off-axis and reached through a bent passage so that no one on the street can see in'). mudejar's own text does not restate the bent-passage detail (its focus is ecclesiastical/civic building, not the domestic courtyard house specifically), but its courtyard-full and townhouse-row massing affinities are consistent with the same convention; the bent-passage clause specifically is carried at judgment-level confidence for the family as a whole rather than asserted as equally sourced for both members.

landscape_idiom.note: Water on the principal axis is a hard, explicit requirement for moorish-andalusian (c05: 'Water is required on the principal axis of any court of consequence... A dry court is a yard') but is not restated anywhere in mudejar's own text, whose typology (churches, towers, civic buildings) is not organised around a residential/palatial water-courtyard in the way the Moorish and vernacular members are. Left open at the family level rather than forced onto a member it is not documented for; belongs on moorish-andalusian's own style kit.
